subject.title: fix(cli): cap config patch file input

question: Should `openclaw config patch --file` now reject patch files over 1 MiB, even though prior file-mode behavior accepted them?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and aligns file mode with the existing stdin limit, but it intentionally removes a previously available CLI workflow for oversized files; code review cannot determine whether that upgrade tradeoff is desired.

options.title: Adopt stdin/file parity
options.body: Accept the 1 MiB limit for both inputs and merge after a current-main refresh, treating large patches as an intentionally unsupported workflow.

options.title: Preserve unlimited file input
options.body: Keep the existing `--file` contract and close or revise this PR if the resource concern does not justify the compatibility break.

options.title: Offer an explicit compatibility path
options.body: Keep the safe default while adding a maintainer-approved documented escape hatch only if large file patches are a supported use case.

recommendation.title: Adopt stdin/file parity
recommendation.body: Accept the 1 MiB limit for both inputs and merge after a current-main refresh, treating large patches as an intentionally unsupported workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product and compatibility decision for a core CLI contract, not a contributor-follow-up defect.
